subject: Predictive pre-warm and prioritized eviction windows for Helium Health Dedicated
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@heliumhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Predictive pre-warm and prioritized eviction windows for Helium Health Dedicated

Hi Lucia / Tom / Procurement team,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — great discussion on expected launch traffic and latency SLAs. Per our conversation, I sketched a practical Dedicated plan to ensure your production traffic stays within latency SLOs during the upcoming MLP on 2029-05-15. Attached is a high-level cost sensitivity spreadsheet (prewarm-costs.xlsx). Key proposals: 

- Predictive pre-warm windows: schedule pre-warm starts at T-4 hours and T-1 hour for the main launch, plus an automated anomaly trigger if traffic ramps >50% above baseline for 10 consecutive minutes. Pre-warm actions will include model weights pinned on GPU hosts, KV cache seed for top prompt prefixes, and inflight batching warmup.
- Prioritized eviction windows: define a "soft eviction" policy during the launch window (10 minute grace for jobs to finish, then soft-preemption of noncritical batch jobs) and a hard-eviction fallback only if capacity falls below safety headroom.
- Billing: we recommend converting pre-warm consumption into reserved credit buckets for the launch month rather than direct pay-as-you-go; this avoids surprise invoices but preserves accounting transparency.

What we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) Expected QPS per endpoint during peak 15-minute window (or example load test trace)
2) Percent of requests requiring long-context (8k+) and model variant mapping (which model names you intend to use)
3) Any hard SLA targets we should bake into autoscaler soft limits

Next steps: if you can share the 15-minute peak estimate and confirmation on model variants by EOD Friday I can have Karthik produce a technical pre-warm runbook and a final pricing sketch.

Best,

Soojin Lee
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: prewarm-costs.xlsx (spreadsheet with hourly pre-warm cost scenarios)

From: Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@heliumhealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@heliumhealth.com>, Tom Hwang <tom.hwang@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Apr 2029 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Predictive pre-warm and prioritized eviction windows for Helium Health Dedicated

Thanks Soojin — this looks sensible and aligns with our expectations. A few clarifying items from procurement and product: 

- Costing: procurement would like an option where pre-warm hours are captured as a fixed monthly credit (we prefer that to an hourly pass-through). Can you outline a credit conversion (e.g., X pre-warm hours = Y reserved credits) and a fallback line item if we exceed the credit?
- Timeline: our MLP (national launch) is 2029-05-15 UTC; we expect sustained elevated traffic from 05-15T16:00Z through 05-15T20:00Z. Peak 15-minute QPS estimate from our preliminary load test is 680 QPS to the primary inference route; ~12% of calls use the long-context model.
- Compliance: any pre-warm materialization that persists cached customer content must meet our retention limits; we will need a short note on cache eviction guarantees.

Looping Tom (platform) for the engineering details. We will send a procurement contact in a separate thread for PO/invoice cadence.

— Lucia
Product Ops, Helium Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lucia Gomez <lucia.gomez@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Predictive pre-warm and prioritized eviction windows for Helium Health Dedicated

Thanks for the data point, Lucia — the 680 QPS peak and 12% long-context mix are helpful. A few technical notes and a recommended autoscale policy we can include in the runbook: 

- Sizing estimate (rough): to meet 99th percentile latency of 200ms for the primary route using model-rw-8k we need a sustained capacity equivalent to ~28 active tokens-per-second GPUs for the 15-minute peak. With the long-context overhead (12%) and typical batch-flooring we recommend pre-warming an additional safety slab equivalent to 6 GPUs (so pre-warm = 34 GPUs) starting at T-1 hour and a lighter pre-warm at T-4 hours of ~10 GPUs for cache seeding.
- Pre-warm work: we will (a) pin the model shard(s) to the reserved slab, (b) pre-populate KV cache for the top 150 prefixes from your logs, (c) spin up the batching agents and run synthetic warmup traffic for 20 minutes to stabilize latency percentiles.
- Triggering: combine three triggers for pre-warm start — calendar scheduled (T-4/T-1), metric anomaly (50% above baseline sustained for 10m), and manual ops action. That gives us predictable pre-warm while allowing rapid manual uplift.
- Prioritized eviction: implement a 2-tier priority queue (critical realtime routes vs background batch jobs). During the soft eviction window (launch + 2 hours), background jobs receive a 10 minute drain window before eviction. If headroom falls below 8% we escalate to hard eviction which preempts any job without SLA lock.
- Cache retention: cached customer inputs will be marked ephemeral; KV entries created for pre-warm must be dropped at T+24h unless explicitly retained by Helium for debugging. This satisfies your retention ask.

I attached a short proposal draft that converts these actions into a runbook for operations. I also included parameterized knobs so we can tune GPU counts once we see the actual load test traces.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposal-draft.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 02 Apr 2029 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Predictive pre-warm and prioritized eviction windows for Helium Health Dedicated

Quick commercial note — appreciate the technical breakdown. A couple of recommended options for Helium to avoid surprise spend and keep accounting simple: 

1) Reserved pre-warm credit: offer a fixed slot "Launch Credit" that converts 240 pre-warm GPU-hours into X reserved credits at a 25% discount to on-demand pre-warm billing. If they consume less we roll the remainder into an operations credit to be used for subsequent months.
2) Overage protection: once credits are exhausted, we provide a 12-hour emergency buffer billed at on-demand rates but with automated alerts to procurement and a kill-switch.
3) Contract clause suggestion: include a one-off SLA exception for the MLP launch window that guarantees pre-warm ramp timing and a single-run remediation credit if runway missed.

I'll draft the clause and add to the proposal. Also recommend a short runbook: who does the manual trigger, slack flywheel, and escalation path to infra on-call. Karthik — can you add the manual ops command and the oncall escalation link to the proposal draft?

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Solutions, Redwood Inference
